question: In the generation of hybridomas by conventional methodology, the presence of aminopterin in the selection medium is intended to inhibit the synthesis of:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Aminopterin -> inhibits dihydrofolate reductase -> inhibits purine synthesis -> 95% CHAIN: Aminopterin -> disrupts nucleotide synthesis -> inhibits purine and pyrimidine synthesis -> 90% CHAIN: Aminopterin -> blocks de novo purine biosynthesis -> inhibits purine production -> 95%
analysis: Aminopterin is a competitive inhibitor of dihydrofolate reductase, an enzyme involved in the synthesis of purines and pyrimidines. By inhibiting this enzyme, aminopterin blocks the de novo synthesis of purines, which are essential components of DNA and RNA. This leads to the inhibition of cell proliferation and ultimately the inhibition of antibody synthesis in hybridomas.
